deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a fair-copy prose passage in German Kurrent on ancient history: the reign of Alexander the Great, apparently from lecture or school notes. It continues directly from the previous page, which ends 'Er hatte Aristoteles zum' and is completed here by 'Lehrer.'

Content, in order:
(1) After Philip's death many subject peoples thought they could regain their independence, so unrest broke out among the Illyrians, Greeks and Thracians.
(2) Alexander first beat the Thracians, crossed the Danube himself and secured his frontiers.
(3) There he heard of an uprising in Thebes. He hurried there with the greatest speed, besieged and stormed the city. More than 6000 inhabitants were cut down, the rest were enslaved and the city was destroyed.
(4) He then held an assembly of the Greeks on the Isthmus (of Corinth), where he declared himself general commander in the Persian war.
(5) He handed affairs in Europe over to Antipater.

The next page continues with the army of 40,000 men, the crossing to Asia in 334, Darius III, Memnon and the Granicus.

These facts match standard ancient sources (Arrian, Diodorus) for 336–335 BC: the Triballian and Getic campaign across the Danube, the destruction of Thebes in 335 with about 6000 killed and about 30,000 enslaved, the League of Corinth, and Antipater as regent. The page has nothing to derive. The hand and genre suggest school or lecture notes, possibly not by Gauss himself; that cannot be decided from the image.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors.

Historically the passage is broadly accurate. 'Mehr als 6 tausend' agrees with the traditional figure of 6000 Theban dead (Diodorus 17.14). The Isthmus assembly corresponds to the League of Corinth confirming Alexander as hegemon/strategos autokrator, a synod usually described as held at Corinth.

results.usually_credited_to: Standard classical sources (Arrian, Diodorus Siculus, Plutarch)
